evidence.quote: Central banks must take their own counsel when deciding upon the timing and force in removing monetary policy accommodation.
Central banks that desire just a little more inflation may well end up with a lot more.
In changing the goal posts at this time of consequence, substantial harm would be done to a central bank's institutional credibility, and perhaps lead to an unmooring of inflation expectations.
Unemployment remains high, and stubbornly so.
Monetary accommodation from the world's largest central banks remains extraordinary.

parsed.rationale: The speech focuses on central bank independence and credibility, warning against keeping policy looser longer and against raising inflation targets, which gives a moderately hawkish tilt. The hawkish tilt is tempered by its acknowledgment of high unemployment and soft medium-term growth.
